s0201.literal: Grandfather Sengbao was Liang attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and groom of the heir apparent.
s0201.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengbao was Liang attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and groom of the heir apparent.

s0202.literal: Father Zhongyue was Liang recording adviser to the Prince of Luling's household and bureau director of sacrifices in the masters of writing.
s0202.idiomatic: His father Zhongyue was Liang recording adviser to the prince of Luling's household and bureau director of sacrifices in the masters of writing.

s0203.literal: Ji from youth was clever and sharp, with thoughtful discernment; at age fourteen he had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
s0203.idiomatic: Ji was clever and sharp from youth, with thoughtful discernment; at fourteen he had mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

s0204.literal: He deeply loved dark learning, studied under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan, and whenever he had a fresh insight elders acknowledged and deferred to him.
s0204.idiomatic: He deeply loved xuanxue, studied under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan, and whenever he had a fresh insight the elders deferred to him.

s0205.literal: In the Datong era of Liang he was summoned and appointed regular student of the Imperial University.
s0205.idiomatic: In Liang's Datong era he was summoned as a regular student of the imperial university.

s0206.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang once at Wendé Hall explained the Wenyan sections of Qian and Kun; Ji together with Yuan Xian of Chen commandery and others were present. An edict ordered debate; none of the scholars dared speak first. Ji composed himself and advanced, inquiry and examination going round and round, his words warm and refined.
s0206.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang once explained the Wenyan on Qian and Kun at Wendé Hall; Ji was there with Yuan Xian of Chen commandery and others. An edict ordered debate, but none of the scholars dared speak first. Ji composed himself and advanced; inquiry went round and round, his words warm and refined.

s0207.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang was greatly struck, granted skirts, robes, silk and the like, and said, "This shows your power in examining antiquity."
s0207.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was greatly struck, granted skirts, robes, and silk, and said, "This shows your power in examining antiquity."

s0208.literal: Ji lost his mother young; there was a patched colorful sutra cloth—his mother's handiwork. When he came to understand, the household told him fully; each year at the season he would choke over the cloth, unable to master himself.
s0208.idiomatic: Ji lost his mother young. There was a patched colorful sutra cloth his mother had made; when he came to understand, the household told him. Each year at the season he would choke over the cloth, unable to master himself.

s0209.literal: When his father's mourning came due, his observance exceeded the rites.
s0209.idiomatic: When his father's mourning came due, his observance exceeded the rites.

s0210.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned as left regular attendant of the Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom, transferred to field-office adviser, and promoted to scholar of the Forest of Gentlemen hall.
s0210.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned as left regular attendant in the prince of Xiangdong's kingdom, transferred to field-office adviser, and made a scholar of the Forest of Gentlemen hall.

s0211.literal: When Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace he issued from the Forest of Gentlemen a topic on the Classic of Filial Piety; Ji's back-and-forth discourse won high praise, and from then on whenever there was a lecture gathering messengers were always sent to summon Ji.
s0211.idiomatic: When Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace he issued a topic on the Classic of Filial Piety from the Forest of Gentlemen; Ji's back-and-forth discourse won high praise, and from then on every lecture gathering sent for him.

s0212.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, even within the besieged city he still attended the Lament-heir at Wude rear hall lecturing on Laozi and Zhuangzi.
s0212.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, even within the besieged city he still attended the lament-heir at Wude rear hall to lecture on Laozi and Zhuangzi.

s0213.literal: When the Liang regime fell, Ji took a rugged path fleeing danger and in the end never served Jing.
s0213.idiomatic: When the Liang regime fell, Ji fled by a rugged path and never served Jing.

s0214.literal: After Jing was pacified, he served in succession as magistrate of Lin'an.
s0214.idiomatic: After Jing was pacified, he served in turn as magistrate of Lin'an.

s0215.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was made vice director of the court for imperial sacrifices, then transferred to criminal-prison adviser in the Prince of Shixing's household.
s0215.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication he was made vice director of the court for imperial sacrifices, then criminal-prison adviser in the prince of Shixing's household.

s0216.literal: In the Tianchen era he was moved to assistant teacher of the Imperial University.
s0216.idiomatic: In the Tianchen era he was made assistant teacher of the imperial university.

s0217.literal: At that time Zhou Hongzheng was at the national academy and issued a topic on the Book of Changes; Hongzheng's fourth younger brother Hongzhi was also on the lecture seat.
s0217.idiomatic: At that time Zhou Hongzheng was at the national academy and issued a topic on the Book of Changes; his fourth younger brother Hongzhi was also on the lecture seat.

s0218.literal: Ji debated with Hongzheng; Hongzheng was thus subdued. Hongzhi sat upright and raised his voice to help state his reasoning.
s0218.idiomatic: Ji debated with Hongzheng until Hongzheng yielded. Hongzhi sat upright and raised his voice to help state his case.

s0219.literal: Ji then with stern countenance said to Hongzhi: "Today's righteous gathering debates and corrects principles; though one knows brothers rush to each other's aid, you, fourth sir, may not assist."
s0219.idiomatic: Ji then said sternly to Hongzhi, "Today's gathering debates principles. Though brothers rush to each other's aid, you, fourth sir, may not help."

s0220.literal: Hongzhi said, "I assist my master's master—why not?"
s0220.idiomatic: Hongzhi said, "I assist my master's master—why not?"

s0221.literal: The whole assembly took it as mirth.

s0222.literal: Hongzheng once told others: "Whenever I mount the seat and see Zhang Ji in the hall, it makes one stand in awe."
s0222.idiomatic: Hongzheng once said, "Whenever I mount the seat and see Zhang Ji in the hall, it makes one stand in awe."

s0223.literal: In the era of Emperor Gaozong he served in succession as recording secretary to the Prince of Jian'an's household, concurrently eastern-palace scholar, then transferred to recording secretary within the limits for the Prince of Wuling—scholar as before.
s0223.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong he was recording secretary to the prince of Jian'an's household and eastern-palace scholar, then recording secretary within the limits for the prince of Wuling, still a scholar.

s0224.literal: When the Later Ruler was in the Eastern Palace he gathered officials for a banquet; a new jade-handled fly-whisk had just been made. The Later Ruler held it himself and said, "Though today scholars are again thick as a forest, as to who can wield this—only Zhang Ji."
s0224.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler was crown prince he gathered officials for a banquet. A new jade-handled fly-whisk had just been made; he held it and said, "Though scholars today are thick as a forest, only Zhang Ji can wield this."

s0225.literal: He thereupon handed it to Ji in person.
s0225.idiomatic: He thereupon handed it to Ji in person.

s0226.literal: He then had him lecture on Zhuangzi and Laozi at Wenwen Hall; Emperor Gaozong visited the palace to listen and granted one suit of his own robes.
s0226.idiomatic: He then had Ji lecture on Zhuangzi and Laozi at Wenwen Hall; Emperor Gaozong visited the palace to listen and granted one suit of his own robes.

s0227.literal: When the Later Ruler succeeded he headed advising secretary to the Prince of Nanping's household and eastern-palace scholar.
s0227.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler succeeded he was advising secretary to the prince of Nanping's household and eastern-palace scholar.

s0228.literal: Soon he was moved to erudite of the Imperial University; scholar as before.
s0228.idiomatic: Soon he was made erudite of the imperial university, still a scholar.

s0229.literal: The Later Ruler once visited Kaishan Temple on Zhongshan, summoned followers to sit in the pine grove southwest of the temple, and ordered Ji summoned to set forth the doctrine.
s0229.idiomatic: The Later Ruler once visited Kaishan Temple on Zhongshan, had his followers sit in the pine grove southwest of the temple, and ordered Ji to set forth the doctrine.

s0230.literal: When the sought fly-whisk had not arrived, the Later Ruler ordered a pine branch taken and with his hand gave it to Ji, saying "It can replace the fly-whisk."
s0230.idiomatic: When the fly-whisk had not arrived, the Later Ruler ordered a pine branch taken and gave it to Ji, saying, "It can replace the fly-whisk."

s0231.literal: Turning to the assembled ministers he said, "This is Zhang Ji's business for afterward."
s0231.idiomatic: Turning to the ministers he said, "This is Zhang Ji's business hereafter."

s0232.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered Sui and died at Chang'an, aged seventy-six.
s0232.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui and died at Chang'an, aged seventy-six.

s0233.literal: Ji's nature was tranquil; he sought no glory or profit and often yearned for leisure. His residence had hills and pools laid out, flowers and fruit planted; there he lectured on the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi and instructed.
s0233.idiomatic: Ji was tranquil by nature and sought no glory or profit, often yearning for leisure. His residence had hills and pools and flowers and fruit; there he lectured on the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi.

s0234.literal: Lu Yuanlang of Wu commandery, Zhu Mengbo, the monk Facai of Yicheng Temple, the monk Huixiu of Fayun Temple, [15] and the Daoist priest Yao Sui of Zhizhen Abbey—all transmitted his learning.
s0234.idiomatic: Lu Yuanlang of Wu commandery, Zhu Mengbo, the monk Facai of Yicheng Temple, the monk Huixiu of Fayun Temple, [15] and the Daoist priest Yao Sui of Zhizhen Abbey—all transmitted his learning.

s0235.literal: Works Ji composed: Meaning of the Zhou Changes 30 juan, Meaning of the Documents 15, Meaning of the Mao Odes 20, Meaning of the Filial Classic 8, Meaning of the Analects 20, Meaning of Laozi 11, Inner Chapters of Zhuangzi 12, Outer Chapters 20, Miscellaneous Chapters 10, Comprehensive Meaning of the Mystic Canon 12; he also composed Roaming the Mystic Cassia Grove 24. The Later Ruler once ordered someone to copy them from his home into the secret archive.
s0235.idiomatic: Ji wrote Meaning of the Zhou Changes in 30 juan, Meaning of the Documents in 15, Meaning of the Mao Odes in 20, Meaning of the Filial Classic in 8, Meaning of the Analects in 20, Meaning of Laozi in 11, Inner Chapters of Zhuangzi in 12, Outer Chapters in 20, Miscellaneous Chapters in 10, and Comprehensive Meaning of the Mystic Canon in 12; he also wrote Roaming the Mystic Cassia Grove in 24. The Later Ruler once ordered them copied from his home into the secret archive.

s0236.literal: His son Xiaozhe rose to recording secretary to the Prince of Shi'an.
s0236.idiomatic: His son Xiaozhe rose to recording secretary to the prince of Shi'an.

s0237.literal: Gu Yue, styled Sinan, [16] was a native of Yanguan in Wu commandery.
s0237.idiomatic: Gu Yue, styled Sinan, [16] was from Yanguan in Wu commandery.

s0238.literal: Where he lived was Xinpo Huangang; for generations there had been a village school, and thus the Gu clan had many Confucian scholars.
s0238.idiomatic: He lived at Xinpo Huangang, where for generations there had been a village school; thus the Gu clan produced many Confucian scholars.

s0239.literal: At the time there was Gong Mengshu of Dongyang, who also studied the Mao Odes and excelled at discussing principles of names.
s0239.idiomatic: At the time Gong Mengshu of Dongyang also studied the Mao Odes and excelled at discussing principles of names.

s0240.literal: In the era of Emperor Wu of Liang he rose to assistant magistrate of Xunyang commandery; when Emperor Yuan was at Jiangzhou he esteemed him greatly and personally took him as teacher.
s0240.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Liang he rose to assistant magistrate of Xunyang; when Emperor Yuan was at Jiangzhou he esteemed him greatly and took him as teacher in person.

s0241.literal: In the Chengsheng era he concurrently served as palace scribe.
s0241.idiomatic: In the Chengsheng era he concurrently served as palace scribe.

s0242.literal: At the beginning of Tianchen he was made supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, concurrently assistant teacher of the Imperial University and grand master for supervision of the army.
s0242.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianchen he was made supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, concurrently assistant teacher of the imperial university and grand master for supervision of the army.

s0243.literal: He died in the Taijian era.
s0243.idiomatic: He died in the Taijian era.

s0245.literal: Shen Buhai, styled Xiaohe, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
s0245.idiomatic: Shen Buhai, styled Xiaohe, was from Wukang in Wuxing.

s0246.literal: Grandfather Zong was Qi director of sacrifices in the masters of writing.
s0246.idiomatic: His grandfather Zong was Qi director of sacrifices in the masters of writing.

s0247.literal: Father Yi was a Liang staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling.
s0247.idiomatic: His father Yi was a Liang staff officer to the prince of Shaoling.

s0248.literal: Buhai was orphaned young yet cultivated himself and loved learning.
s0248.idiomatic: Buhai was orphaned young yet cultivated himself and loved learning.

s0249.literal: At fourteen he was summoned as student of the Imperial University and nominated for mastery of the classics.
s0249.idiomatic: At fourteen he was summoned as a student of the imperial university and nominated for mastery of the classics.

s0250.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Liang grand-academy doctor, then transferred to criminal-prison adviser in the Prince of Luling's household, advising secretary to the Prince of Changsha, and concurrently magistrate of Runan.
s0250.idiomatic: He rose to Liang grand-academy doctor, then criminal-prison adviser in the prince of Luling's household, advising secretary to the prince of Changsha, and concurrently magistrate of Runan.

s0251.literal: At the beginning of Tianchen he was made middle recording secretary to the Prince of Hengyang's household and concurrently scholar of the Hall of Excellent Virtue.
s0251.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianchen he was made middle recording secretary to the prince of Hengyang's household and scholar of the Hall of Excellent Virtue.

s0252.literal: From the disorders at the end of Liang until then the national academy had not been established; Buhai submitted a memorial saying:
s0252.idiomatic: From the disorders at the end of Liang until then the national academy had not been established; Buhai submitted a memorial saying:

s0253.literal: Your servant has heard that in establishing persons and founding states, nothing surpasses honoring Confucian scholars; in completing customs and transforming the people, one must exalt teaching and learning.
s0253.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that in establishing persons and founding states nothing surpasses honoring Confucian scholars, and in completing customs and transforming the people one must exalt teaching and learning.

s0254.literal: Thus the eastern glue and western school—affairs reached their height in the Three Dynasties; the ringed forest and jade water—the enterprise flourished in the Two Capitals.
s0254.idiomatic: Thus the eastern glue and western school reached their height in the Three Dynasties, and the ringed forest and jade water flourished in the Two Capitals.

s0255.literal: Since the pure source had grown distant and the shallow wave had already risen, the myriad things' power to move people is inexhaustible and people's pursuit of desire knows no bounds—therefore one sets instruction and hangs models, opens and guides the mind, like dyeing in indigo or like carving jade; only then are human relations made harmonious, high and low given order, the principle of loyalty and filial piety made clear, and the way of ruler and minister made firm.
s0255.idiomatic: Since the pure source had grown distant and shallow ways had risen, things move people without end and desire knows no bounds. Therefore one sets instruction and models, opens and guides the mind, like dyeing in indigo or carving jade; only then are human relations harmonious, high and low ordered, loyalty and filial piety clear, and the way of ruler and minister firm.

s0256.literal: Taking ritual as foundation—the Duke of Lu was therefore hard to insult; when song and music had grown minute, the Earl of Zheng thereupon perished first; when shield and axes were danced the Miao came; when the pan-palace was completed the Huai Yi submitted—long to think on the wind of Zhu and Si, fully to cherish the flourishing of Yan and Ji: states and families, none but honored it.
s0256.idiomatic: Taking ritual as foundation, the Duke of Lu was hard to insult; when song and music grew minute, the Earl of Zheng perished; when shield and axes were danced the Miao came; when the pan-palace was completed the Huai Yi submitted. Long to recall the wind of Zhu and Si and the flourishing of Yan and Ji—states and families all honored it.

s0257.literal: In the last years of Liang's Taiqing era, misfortune repeatedly struck; barbarians invaded from without, wicked factions rebelled within; in the morning drums and gongs were heard, by evening beacon fires shone.
s0257.idiomatic: In the last years of Liang's Taiqing era misfortune struck again and again; barbarians invaded from without and wicked factions rebelled within; drums and gongs were heard in the morning, beacon fires by evening.

s0258.literal: Great Confucians and broad scholars were scattered worse than the pit-martyrs; the Five Classics and Nine Sections were effaced more than under a canopy-screen.
s0258.idiomatic: Great Confucians and broad scholars were scattered worse than the pit-martyrs; the Five Classics and Nine Sections were lost worse than under a canopy.

s0259.literal: The accomplished mean from then cast its work down; the blind-director shrine was thereupon not repaired; the shrine of Bao Cheng offered no libation-sacrifice; the rite of presenting vegetables had no claim on ritual vessels; hymnody fell silent—for more than twelve years.
s0259.idiomatic: The accomplished mean then cast down its work; the blind-director shrine went unrepaired; the shrine of Bao Cheng offered no libation; the rite of presenting vegetables had no vessels; hymnody fell silent for more than twelve years.

s0260.literal: Later students delighted in learning but did not see the ritual of bearing the writing tablet; late scholars drilled and looked up, yet only deepened the sigh of leaning on the mat.
s0260.idiomatic: Later students delighted in learning but never saw the ritual of bearing the writing tablet; late scholars drilled and looked up, yet only sighed at leaning on the mat.

s0261.literal: Your Majesty has succeeded to the calendar and mounted the throne, holding the mirror and overlooking the realm; the Way has penetrated within the seas, authority extends beyond all borders; turbid currents are already clear, heavy mists are greatly dispersed; the living flourish on high mounds, all ranks enjoy prosperity.
s0261.idiomatic: Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne and holds the mirror over the realm; the Way fills the seas and authority extends beyond all borders; turbid currents are clear and heavy mists dispersed; the living flourish and all ranks prosper.

s0262.literal: It is fitting to grandly revive ritual and music, establish schools and academies, model antiquity's rules, linger with footprints at the Confucian palace, select sons of dukes and ministers—all to enter study; assistant teachers and erudites to lecture morning and evening—so that those who shoulder book-boxes and carry satchels rustle garment to garment, square-collared and measured in step, press thick as a forest.
s0262.idiomatic: It is fitting to revive ritual and music grandly, establish schools, model antiquity, and dwell at the Confucian palace, selecting sons of dukes and ministers for study, with assistant teachers and erudites lecturing morning and evening, so that those who shoulder book-boxes and carry satchels press thick as a forest, square-collared and measured in step.

s0263.literal: As if cutting, as if polishing; hearing the Odes, hearing the Rites—one year can double the work; three winters then suffice for use.
s0263.idiomatic: As if cutting, as if polishing; hearing the Odes and Rites—one year doubles the work, three winters suffice for use.

s0264.literal: Thus one can raise excellence in a commandery, raise one's name in court and observe the state; enter office and ascend court, relying on superior learning to aid oneself; take office and govern, having classic learning to order the person—carriages fill the court, blue and purple are gathered from the ground.
s0264.idiomatic: Thus one can raise excellence in a commandery and one's name at court; enter office and ascend court aided by superior learning; take office and govern with classic learning to order the person—carriages fill the court and blue and purple are gathered from the ground.

s0265.literal: In antiquity the crown prince's nobility still ranked with the sons of the state; down to the Han heir this ritual did not fall; reaching the two Jin, this matter grew even more exalted—thus one sees the teacher honored and the Way respected.
s0265.idiomatic: In antiquity the crown prince's nobility still ranked with the sons of the state; down to the Han heir this ritual did not fall; in the two Jin it grew more exalted—thus the teacher is honored and the Way respected.

s0266.literal: The crown prince is heaven-bestowed with innate knowledge and needs no repeated explanation—yet he should still conceal his traces and bow level with others, specialize in the classics and request instruction, set forth the libation cup before the teacher, solemn as the old canon.
s0266.idiomatic: The crown prince is heaven-bestowed with innate knowledge and needs no repeated explanation, yet he should still bow level with others, specialize in the classics and request instruction, and set forth the libation cup before the teacher, solemn as the old canon.

s0267.literal: Formerly in the hall at Que Li, Mo Lai opened his own path; within the old dwelling, silk and bamboo streamed with sound—the former sage's legacy warns sharply.
s0267.idiomatic: Formerly in the hall at Que Li, Mo Lai opened his own path; within the old dwelling silk and bamboo streamed—the former sage's legacy warns sharply.

s0268.literal: Moreover the lands south of the Yangtze are without care, beyond the seas are cut off—how can one fail to open and spread the great plan, extend and magnify the utmost Way?
s0268.idiomatic: Moreover the lands south of the Yangtze are secure and the seas are cut off—how can one fail to open the great plan and extend the utmost Way?

s0269.literal: Could one allow the dark teaching and Confucian wind not to rise in a sage age, great virtue and great enterprise to lie hidden in Yao's years?
s0269.idiomatic: Could one allow the dark teaching and Confucian wind not to rise in a sage age, or great virtue and great enterprise to lie hidden like Yao's years?

s0270.literal: Your servant, a petty late student, words not worth reckoning, lightly offers blind words and increases dread bowed low.
s0270.idiomatic: Your servant, a petty late student whose words are not worth reckoning, lightly offers blind counsel and bows in dread.

s0271.literal: An edict replied: "Your memorial has been read."
s0271.idiomatic: An edict replied, "Your memorial has been read."

s0272.literal: "Since old regulations were relaxed and abandoned, subtle words were about to perish; We have succeeded to the precious enterprise and Our thought is in drawing brightness close—yet arms have not ceased and army and state are still newly founded; We constantly fear the former kings' ordered canon may in a morning be extinguished."
s0272.idiomatic: "Since old regulations were abandoned, subtle words were about to perish. We have succeeded to the precious enterprise and seek to draw brightness close, yet arms have not ceased and army and state are still newly founded; We constantly fear the former kings' ordered canon may be extinguished in a morning."

s0273.literal: "Your talent and thought are excellent and harmonious, your wen and li can be sought; broadly cherish the great body, earnestly attend the teaching of names—deliver to outside for detailed deliberation and implement according to affairs."
s0273.idiomatic: "Your talent and thought are excellent, your wen and li can be sought; broadly cherish the great body and earnestly attend the teaching of names—deliver outside for detailed deliberation and implement according to affairs."

s0274.literal: He also memorialized to revise and fix ritual hymns; an edict had him compose eight three-court music songs, twenty-eight pieces in all, implemented at the Music Office.
s0274.idiomatic: He also memorialized to revise ritual hymns; an edict had him compose eight three-court music songs, twenty-eight pieces in all, for the Music Office.

s0275.literal: In year 5 he was made magistrate of Gan.
s0275.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made magistrate of Gan.

s0276.literal: He entered service as bureau director of ceremonies in the masters of writing, was moved to erudite of the Imperial University, headed the Feathered Forest guard, was ordered to compile the five rites, and managed draft texts for posthumous titles.
s0276.idiomatic: He entered service as bureau director of ceremonies in the masters of writing, became erudite of the imperial university, headed the feathered forest guard, was ordered to compile the five rites, and managed draft texts for posthumous titles.

s0277.literal: In the Taijian era he was made chief steward to the Prince of Renwu, heir of Nan and Kang, and acted in the affairs of Danyang commandery.
s0277.idiomatic: In the Taijian era he was chief steward to the prince of Renwu, heir of Nan and Kang, and acted in Danyang affairs.

s0278.literal: He was transferred to supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and minister of the household for the imperial clan.
s0278.idiomatic: He was transferred to supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and minister of the household for the imperial clan.

s0279.literal: Soon he was made martial-proclamation general and chief steward to the Prince of Mingwu in Wuling, acting in the affairs of Wuxing commandery.
s0279.idiomatic: Soon he was martial-proclamation general and chief steward to the prince of Mingwu in Wuling, acting in Wuxing affairs.

s0280.literal: Shortly he entered service as attendant-in-ordinary for direct communication and concurrently left assistant in the masters of writing.
s0280.idiomatic: Shortly he entered service as attendant-in-ordinary for direct communication and left assistant in the masters of writing.

s0281.literal: In year 12 he died, aged sixty-three.
s0281.idiomatic: In year 12 he died, aged sixty-three.

s0282.literal: Buhai mastered classic learning and excelled at composition; though broadly versed in the canonical tomes, his home had no scrolls.
s0282.idiomatic: Buhai mastered the classics and excelled at composition; though broadly versed in the canonical tomes, his home had no scrolls.

s0283.literal: Whenever he composed a text he took up the brush and finished at once, never needing to search or check.
s0283.idiomatic: Whenever he composed he took up the brush and finished at once, never needing to search or check.

s0284.literal: Vice Director Zhou Hongzheng of Runan always praised him, saying: "Master Shen may be called a sage of ideas!
s0284.idiomatic: Vice director Zhou Hongzheng of Runan always said, "Master Shen may be called a sage of ideas!

s0285.literal: " He authored Correcting the Five Rites Protocols in one hundred juan and a collected writings in fourteen juan.
s0285.idiomatic: " He wrote Correcting the Five Rites Protocols in one hundred juan and collected writings in fourteen juan.

s0286.literal: His son Zhidao, styled Chongji, was known from youth.
s0286.idiomatic: His son Zhidao, styled Chongji, was known from youth.

s0287.literal: On first appointment he was registrar of Yangzhou; soon he concurrently served as Palace Forest scholar and in succession was recording secretary to the Prince of Andong in Xin.
s0287.idiomatic: On first appointment he was registrar of Yangzhou; soon he was also a Palace Forest scholar and recording secretary to the prince of Andong in Xin.

s0288.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he entered Sui.
s0288.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui.

s0290.literal: Wang Yuangui, styled Zhengfan, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
s0290.idiomatic: Wang Yuangui, styled Zhengfan, was from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

s0291.literal: Grandfather Daobao, [20] was Qi supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and administrator of Jin'an commandery.
s0291.idiomatic: His grandfather Daobao, [20] was Qi supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry and administrator of Jin'an commandery.

s0292.literal: Father Wei was middle recording secretary to the Prince of Wuling's household.
s0292.idiomatic: His father Wei was middle recording secretary to the prince of Wuling's household.

s0293.literal: Yuangui was orphaned at eight; three brothers followed their mother to rely on a maternal uncle's clan and went to Linhai commandery when he was twelve.
s0293.idiomatic: Yuangui was orphaned at eight; he and his two brothers followed their mother to their uncle's house in Linhai commandery when he was twelve.

s0294.literal: A local magnate of the commandery, Liu Zhen, had wealth in the tens of millions and gave him his daughter in marriage.
s0294.idiomatic: A local magnate, Liu Zhen, had wealth in the tens of millions and offered his daughter in marriage.

s0295.literal: Yuangui's mother, because the brothers were young and weak, wished to secure a powerful ally; Yuangui wept and pleaded, saying: "Marriage must not lose kin—[21] ancients held it weighty.
s0295.idiomatic: Yuangui's mother, because the brothers were young, wished to secure a powerful ally; Yuangui wept and pleaded, "Marriage must not lose kin—[21] ancients held it weighty.

s0296.literal: How can one for ease in a foreign land rashly marry outside one's kind!
s0296.idiomatic: How can one for ease in a foreign land rashly marry outside one's kind!

s0297.literal: " His mother was moved by his words and stopped.
s0297.idiomatic: " His mother was moved and stopped.

s0298.literal: Yuangui was filial by nature and served his mother with utmost care; morning and evening he never left her side.
s0298.idiomatic: Yuangui was filial by nature and served his mother with utmost care, never leaving her side morning or evening.

s0299.literal: In Liang times Shanyin county had a sudden flood that swept away the dwelling; Yuangui had only one small boat and in haste drew his mother, younger sister, and orphaned nephews into the boat, [22] while Yuangui himself took the oars and went off, leaving three male and female kin lodged in the treetops; when the water receded all were saved, and people of the time all praised his utmost conduct.
s0299.idiomatic: In Liang times a sudden flood in Shanyin swept away their dwelling; Yuangui had only one small boat and in haste put his mother, younger sister, and orphaned nephews aboard, [22] while he himself took the oars and went off, leaving three kin lodged in the treetops; when the water receded all were saved, and people praised his utmost conduct.

s0300.literal: When the Later Ruler was in the Eastern Palace he was summoned as scholar; he personally received instruction in the meanings of the Record of Rites, Zuo Tradition, and Mourning Garments, with generous rewards.
s0300.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler was crown prince he was summoned as scholar and personally received instruction in the Record of Rites, Zuo Tradition, and Mourning Garments, with generous rewards.
